A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same four-mode social-agent framework and AMPO algorithm despite the retitling and AML-to-ASL renaming. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SOTOPIA evaluations, mode ablations, training dynamics, and human comparisons in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds out-of-distribution evaluations, efficient-reasoning comparisons, component ablations, and evaluator checks in Tables 4–9.

M1.justification: The four reasoning action sequences, behavioral cloning followed by single-turn RL, combined mode/sample advantages, and answer/format/length rewards are retained. The ASL renaming, explicit mode-prefix explanation, and revised notation do not establish a substantive change to the optimization or inference procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates SOTOPIA and SOTOPIA-Hard. v5 adds DEMO, including Chinese and English dialogue and more adversarial/non-cooperative scenarios, plus NegotiationArena's Sell&Buy and Ultimatum tasks (Appendix D.1, Tables 4–5). These extend evaluation coverage beyond the original benchmark family; training remains based on SOTOPIA-π.

E2.justification: v5 Table 7 newly compares AMPO against TALE-PT, DeGRPO, LS-Mix, and O1-Pruner on both backbones. In the corresponding main comparison, Table 1 replaces Gemini-2.0-flash-thinking with Gemini-2.5-Pro. The existing social-planning baselines and BC/GRPO comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v5 introduces OOD partner/role-swapping protocols, profit and winning-rate metrics, and evaluations with two alternative LLM judges. Human evaluation changes from 100 sampled dialogues to all episodes from both benchmarks. The reported Llama RL learning rate changes from 1e-7 in v1 Table 5 to 2e-7 in v5 Table 11; this documentation change does not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained single-mode and adaptive-behavior analyses, v5 adds answer-length-reward ablations, state-diversity and marginal-reward ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, and alternative-judge checks (Tables 3, 6, 8–9). It also adds OOD generalization tests and concrete LRM failure traces (Tables 15–18). The original AMPO dialogue case is retained and reformatted.

E5.justification: Both main-result tables report fourfold averaging and p < 0.05. v5 newly reports 73.39% pairwise agreement among human annotators in Appendix I.1. Its expanded ablation table no longer includes v1 Table 2's explicit four-evaluation and significance statement; no increase in main-experiment repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Matched main-table results, apart from the replaced Gemini comparator, and original single-mode ablations retain their numbers. v5 adds substantial results: for example, DEMO averages of 7.81/7.72 for Qwen AMPO/GRPO with GPT-4o (Table 4), and SOTOPIA-Hard GOAL of 7.12 without diverse states versus 7.85 for full AMPO (Table 6). Human win/lose percentages also change under the revised reported sampling, rather than demonstrating a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v5 Section 2.1 adds an explicit POMDP formulation, defining observations, transitions, trajectories, and an expected terminal-reward objective where v1 provides a less formal interaction description. Existing AMPO and reward equations remain equivalent apart from notation and placement. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions—adaptive reasoning modes for social agents and AMPO's performance/token advantages—remain. v5 refines the headline 15.6% comparison to explicitly name GPT-4o rather than broadly referring to state-of-the-art methods, and drops the abstract's explicit claim of more human-like reasoning than GRPO.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive arguments connecting single-turn optimization to long-horizon consistency, interpretations of OOD transfer and efficient-reasoning tradeoffs, and expanded LRM failure explanations. It also discusses training/inference costs and explicitly qualifies alternative-judge results because those judges lack validation against human annotations (Appendices B, D, and K).

D1.justification: v5 newly specifies 4,000 BC examples and 2,057 RL queries, length-reward defaults, detailed BC/RL configurations (Tables 28–29), the SOTOPIA evaluation prompt (Tables 26–27), and adaptations of the new baselines (Appendix H.3). It adds an Apache-2.0 licensing statement. The repository link and eight-A100 hardware disclosure already existed.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands positioning around efficient reasoning, overthinking, social-learning foundations, static versus interactive social benchmarks, and single-turn dialogue training. It explicitly distinguishes AMPO from compression, mixed-length training, and binary-reward approaches. This goes beyond bibliographic updates to retained works such as EPO, DSI, and DEMO.

P1.justification: The title, framework name, and thinking/reasoning terminology change alongside extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and research questions. Standalone preliminaries are removed, the method is reorganized around task formulation, modes, BC, and AMPO, and reward/pseudocode details move into substantially reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: v5 expands the original AMPO diagram into a three-stage framework overview, redraws and relocates the introductory scenario, and reformats the mode-distribution plots. It replaces the separate-benchmark human-results table with one set of bar charts, restructures the ablation table, adds experiment/configuration tables, and spreads the retained dialogue example across three tables.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence for transfer beyond SOTOPIA and efficiency relative to specialized reasoning methods. OOD evaluations, direct efficiency comparisons, targeted ablations, evaluator checks, and fuller implementation details strengthen validation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting shortcomings: human results lose their benchmark breakdown, and Table 7 overstates universal superiority—DeGRPO scores 3.72 versus AMPO's 3.68 on Llama SOTOPIA-Hard self-play OVERALL.
